note:
The FULL-FACE variant of the three clinical-result blocks on /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research - templates/page.research-argireline.json, section `key_findings`, blocks f1, f2, f3. Malcolm, 2026-08-25: the same batch again, but with DIFFERENT WOMEN and the FULL FACE in view in both panels, with a clear difference between before and after in lighting, head position, eye gaze, background and clothes. Earlier rounds (r1, r2, r3 crow's feet; forehead r1/r2; mouth-chin r1/r2) are all kept.

ONE WAVE, NOT THREE. The previous rounds ran a separate wave per facial region. A full face shows forehead, eyes and mouth at once, so the region split collapses - three region waves would differ only by label. Each slot instead keeps its own EMPHASIS matching its trial: f1 the crow's-feet fan, f2 depth read by hard directional light, f3 a fine surface network.

⚠️ THE TRADE-OFF THIS FRAMING BUYS AND WHAT IT COSTS. Live box is 660px wide on desktop and 350px on mobile, split in two, so each face renders about 330px and 175px wide. Crow's feet and fine lines are at the very edge of visibility at that size - which means the percentage plate carries more of the message than the photograph does, the reverse of the macro sets where the change was legible at 350px. Judge these at render size before choosing, per the standing rule. Stated to Malcolm before the wave ran.

SESSION VARIANCE IS NOW LARGER THAN IN r3, BY REQUEST, AND THAT RAISES THE IDENTITY RISK. r3 varied head angle by "a few degrees"; this asks for a noticeably different head position, a different key light direction, a different gaze, a different backdrop tone and a different garment. On r3 the looser brief already let flux2 return a visibly different, older woman in the right panel of one forehead candidate. At full face there is far more of a person to get wrong, so the identity anchors are stated harder here: same face shape and jawline, same nose, same eye colour, same haircut and hair colour, and the permanent marks in the same places. CHECK EVERY CANDIDATE FOR PERSON DRIFT FIRST - it is the failure mode of this wave, ahead of skin quality.

DO NOT LET THE AFTER PANEL BECOME A YOUNGER WOMAN. At full face the engines will happily "improve" her by making her younger, slimmer or prettier. The brief states that she must not appear older or younger, heavier or thinner, and that the same face is simply less deeply creased. `no age progression, no elderly transformation, no weight change` are in the negatives.

INHERITED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING:
  * THE HONESTY DEVICE: the number and position of the lines is the same in both panels, NO LINE MAY DISAPPEAR, only depth and shadow change. Magnitude as a fraction of depth per block - f1 about half, f2 about a third, f3 the smallest but still visible. Session variance applies to the PHOTOGRAPH, never to the FINDING.
  * NO LETTERING FROM ANY ENGINE. Every percentage is composited afterwards by scripts/label-before-after.py. AND A NEW SPECIFIC: r3 proved that NAMING THE PANELS gives an engine words to draw - nbp_pro rendered "FIRST VISIT" and "FOLLOW-UP" into the corners of candidates in two separate waves, because the prompt said "the left panel is the first visit, the right panel is the follow-up". This brief says "the earlier visit" and "the later one" instead, and `no timestamp, no date stamp` stay in the negatives. Check the top corners of every nbp_pro candidate.
  * CAUCASIAN MIDDLE-AGED WOMEN, and THREE NEW INDIVIDUALS - none of them the women used in r3 - so the page never repeats a face and no one woman appears enrolled in three studies.
  * SKIN REALISM SPECIFIED POSITIVELY: pore size varying by zone, individual outsized pores, asymmetric never-mirrored pigmentation, vellus hair, matte-to-oily variation. Sheen, glow, dewy and hydrated stay banned - they render as speckled white highlights that read as dry flaking.
  * ⚠️ SITE OF MEASUREMENT: all three trials measured the PERIORBITAL region. A full-face frame shows the whole face rather than the site measured, so the block copy and alt text must not imply the figure was measured across the face.

COLOUR: Acetyl's scene colour is Pearl grey D8D6D4 - here as the studio backdrop, differing slightly in tone between the two panels, never as a cast on her skin. CLASS B, no references. Square 2048x2048, each panel a 1:2 portrait.
labels_are_composited: scripts/label-before-after.py - see `label` on each slot. The engines never draw text.

slots.title: f1 · Wang 2013 — 48.9% anti-wrinkle efficacy vs 0% placebo, 4 weeks  —  full face, two sessions
slots.prompt:
Two separate unretouched clinical portrait photographs of THE SAME WOMAN, taken WEEKS APART at two different clinic visits, placed side by side to fill one square frame edge to edge: TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH meeting at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre. Each panel is a tall portrait. The left panel is the earlier visit, the right panel is the later one.

HER WHOLE FACE IS IN VIEW IN BOTH PANELS - head and shoulders, the entire face from above the hairline down to the collarbones, nothing cropped off. Both eyes, the nose, the whole mouth and the full jawline are visible in each panel. She looks toward the camera with a calm, neutral, closed-mouth expression at both visits - not smiling, not frowning, not posing.

THESE ARE TWO SESSIONS, NOT TWO COPIES OF ONE FRAME. A real trial cannot pose someone identically weeks later, and a pair that matches perfectly looks retouched. So everything that identifies her stays the same, and everything a second visit would naturally change is different.

UNMISTAKABLY THE SAME WOMAN: the same face shape and jawline, the same nose, the same eye colour, the same brow shape, the same hair colour and the same haircut, and her permanent marks - moles, freckles, sun spots - in the same places on her face. A viewer must be able to look from one panel to the other and be certain it is one person.

CLEARLY DIFFERENT BETWEEN THE TWO VISITS, AND THIS IS THE POINT OF THE PAIR:
  * LIGHTING - the key light comes from a noticeably different side and height, so the shadow under her nose and jaw falls differently and the modelling on her cheeks is not the same.
  * HEAD POSITION - her head is turned and tilted differently in relation to the camera; one panel is more three-quarter and the other closer to straight on, and she sits at a slightly different height in the frame.
  * EYE GAZE - she is looking in a different direction in each panel; in one she meets the lens and in the other her eyes go a little off to one side.
  * BACKGROUND - a different tone of plain studio backdrop in each panel, both pale and quiet, with the light falling across it differently.
  * CLOTHES - a completely different garment at each visit, in a different colour and a different neckline.
  * HAIR - it is the same haircut, but it falls differently: a different parting, strands sitting differently, one loose strand across the face in only one of the panels.

These differences are what make the pair read as two real clinic visits rather than one retouched photograph. But she must never stop being recognisably the same woman, and she must not appear older or younger, heavier or thinner, in one panel than the other.

She is a white woman of about fifty-five, with a silver-grey chin-length bob, cool pale skin and hazel eyes. Her skin carries the marks of a life outdoors: a scatter of sun spots across both cheekbones, one small raised mole beside her left nostril, and visible open pores across the nose and inner cheeks.

WHAT THE COMPARISON IS ABOUT, AND THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE TRUE: the number and position of the expression lines on her face is the same in both panels and NOT ONE OF THEM HAS DISAPPEARED. Her moles and freckles are all still there in the same places. What has changed between the two visits is only HOW DEEP the lines are. She has not been made younger, smoother or more beautiful - the same face is simply less deeply creased.

THE SKIN MUST HOLD UP AS REAL AT FULL SIZE. Pores are clearly visible and vary in size and density by zone - open through the centre of the face and across the nose, much finer at the temples and along the jaw - with several individual pores larger than their neighbours. Pigmentation is uneven and asymmetric, never mirrored from one side of the face to the other. Fine pale vellus hairs catch the light along the jaw and upper lip. The skin is slightly oily and light-catching across the nose and forehead and completely matte at the outer cheeks. She wears no makeup at either visit, so lips, lashes and brows are their own natural colour.

AT THE EARLIER VISIT, in the LEFT panel, her expression lines are deeply set even with her face at rest: a fan of four or five creases spreading from the outer corner of each eye across the temples, three horizontal lines across the forehead, a pair of short vertical creases between the brows, and a distinct line running down from each side of the nose. Each one is folded deeply enough to hold a clear shadow along its length.

AT THE LATER VISIT, in the RIGHT panel, EVERY ONE OF THOSE LINES IS STILL THERE, IN THE SAME PLACES AND THE SAME NUMBER, AND NOT ONE HAS DISAPPEARED. Each is about HALF as deep - the fold softer, the shadow it holds much lighter, its edges less sharply defined. The deepest ones are still plainly visible on her face. Her moles, sun spots and freckles are all still there in the same places.

At the earlier visit a soft key from the upper left with a gentle fill; at the later visit the key sits higher and more to the right and is a touch warmer, so the shadows fall differently across her face. Photographed head-on for a clinical record with a portrait lens, sharp throughout, honest and completely unretouched - a documentary photograph of a real woman, not a beauty campaign.
